summary: The owner pays no North Dakota sales tax on a construction, remodeling or repair contract for real property; the contractor pays sales or use tax on the materials it installs.

citations.title: ND Tax Commissioner, Guideline: Contractors
citations.quote: A contractor or subcontractor entering any contract, except for a labor only contract, is regarded as the final user or consumer of all tangible personal property installed into real property.

citations.title: NDAC 81-04.1-04-20
citations.quote: A contractor or subcontractor installing materials into real property located in North Dakota must pay sales or use tax on those materials regardless of who owns them.

citations.title: ND Tax Commissioner, Guideline: Repair Services
citations.quote: If labor and parts are not itemized or the parts are attached to real property, the repairer must pay tax on the cost of the repair parts and may not charge tax to the customer.

citations.title: NDAC 81-04.1-01-22
citations.quote: Personal and professional services are not subject to sales tax

notes: Both subcodes (improvement and repair) alike: the contractor is the consumer of the materials and the labor is a nontaxable service, so no sales tax is charged to the owner. Since contracts entered after 2021-06-30, a labor-only subcontractor doesn't owe tax on materials it installs (the providing contractor does) — this shifts who pays on materials, not the owner's treatment. A contractor that sells goods without installing them into real property charges sales tax on them.

summary: A seller's delivery charge on goods exempt at that sale (such as groceries) is exempt from North Dakota sales tax.

citations.quote: If the product being delivered is exempt from sales tax, then freight, delivery and other transportation charges are also exempt.

citations.title: NDAC 81-04.1-01-10
citations.quote: If the sale is taxable, the freight, delivery, and other transportation charges that are part of the sale and billed by the seller are taxable. If the product being delivered is exempt from sales tax, then freight, delivery, and other transportation charges are also exempt.

citations.title: ND Tax Commissioner, Guideline: Grocery Stores, Convenience Stores, & Delicatessens (updated 5-2026)
citations.quote: If the sale is taxable, the freight, delivery, and other transportation charges are taxable. If the product being delivered is exempt from sales tax, then the freight, delivery, and other transportation charges are also exempt.

notes: For mixed shipments the seller allocates by price or weight (NDCC 57-39.2-01, 'Delivery charges').

summary: Groceries (food and food ingredients) are exempt from North Dakota sales tax.

summary: Bakery items sold without eating utensils provided by the seller are exempt food in North Dakota.

conditions.when: The seller's prepared food ratio is above 75% and utensils are made available (e.g. a café or coffee shop), so utensils count as provided

citations.title: NDCC 57-39.2-04.1(2)(e)(3)(c)
citations.quote: (c) Bakery items, including bread, rolls, buns, biscuits, bagels, croissants, pastries, donuts, Danish, cakes, tortes, pies, tarts, muffins, bars, cookies, and tortillas.

citations.title: ND Tax Commissioner, Guideline: Grocery Stores, Convenience Stores, & Delicatessens (updated 5-2026)
citations.quote: Bakery items are not taxable unless they are sold with eating utensils by the seller.

notes: The bakery exclusion applies only 'if sold without eating utensils provided by the seller'; for a seller whose prepared food ratio exceeds 75%, utensils made available count as provided (NDCC 57-39.2-04.1(3)(c)), so an individual pastry at a restaurant is taxable (the Restaurants guideline taxes items sold for immediate consumption). ND follows the SSUTA prepared-food definition (NDCC 57-39.2-04.1). Whether utensils count as 'provided by the seller' turns on the seller's prepared food ratio: above 75%, utensils merely made available count (NDCC 57-39.2-04.1(3)). NDAC 81-04.1-03-03 was last amended 2016-07-01; earlier history not checked.
